title: Sosulski et al. 2019 — Online Optimization of Stimulation Speed in an Auditory Brain-Computer Interface under Time Constraints
description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an auditory oddball (P300) paradigm with target (1000 Hz) and non-target (500 Hz) tones at various stimulus onset asynchronies (60-600 ms). The data were collected to evaluate closed-loop optimization of stimulation speed, comparing random search and Bayesian optimization of the SOA to maximize regularized LDA classification performance. The dataset contains 31-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz, with an optimization part and a validation part.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG (BrainProducts BrainAmp DC, passive Ag/AgCl, nose reference, 1000 Hz) was recorded during an auditory oddball task. The optimization part ran four strategies (AUC-ucb, AUC-rand, P300-ucb, P300-rand) for 20 minutes each. The validation part tested the selected SOAs and a fixed 60 ms SOA over 20 trials each. Features were mean amplitudes in 5 time intervals across channels, classified with shrinkage rLDA using 13-fold cross-validation.
